topic: Three credits people miss: eligible educator school supply credit, Canada training credit, home accessibility tax credit (federal, tax year 2026)

example.note: example family; CTC room assumes she met the conditions (age 26–65, filed, resident, working income threshold, income limit) every year 2019–2025, so $250 accrued for each of 2020–2026; mom must owe at least $2,800 of federal tax to use the full non-refundable credit

derive.total: min(supplies, edu_cap) * edu_rate + min(min(ctc_per_year * ctc_years, ctc_lifetime), course * 0.5) + round(min(reno, hatc_cap) * rate)

spoken.total: four thousand, five hundred and fifty dollars

sources.educator: ITA 122.9(1)-(2): eligible educator (teacher or ECE employed at an elementary/secondary school or regulated child care facility, with a recognized certificate) is deemed to have paid 25% of the lesser of $1,000 and eligible supplies expenses (refundable); employer certificate on request (122.9(3))
sources.ctc: ITA 122.91(1)-(2): refundable credit = lesser of the training amount limit and 50% of eligible tuition; limit grows $250 a year after 2019 (age 26–65 at year end, return filed and resident in the prior year, working income threshold, income not above the 117(2)(c) amount), lifetime $5,000; ITA 118.5(1.2): tuition credit reduced by 14% × the CTC claimed; canada.ca line 45350: the limit is shown on the latest notice of (re)assessment and in My Account
sources.hatc: ITA 118.041: credit = appropriate percentage × lesser of $20,000 and qualifying expenditures; qualifying individual = 65+ at year end or DTC-eligible; renovation must be enduring and let the person gain access / be mobile / reduce risk of harm (non-refundable)
